finding: Unused sign-voting parameters prevent candidate/group-cache deduplication
status: reproduced; not fixed in the frozen benchmark implementation

synthetic_cpu_probe.procedure: Load tests/test_lora_optimizer.py using importlib.util.spec_from_file_location to provide only Comfy stubs; force _get_compute_device to CPU. Call the actual LoRAOptimizer._decide_prefix_mode for each strategy set and supplied synthetic statistics, with smoothing/full-rank flags false. Compare the first three returned fields used by the actual _strategy_signature. Compare actual _group_merge_cache_key results with refinement none, sparsification disabled, density 0.7, dampening 0 and auto_strength enabled. Call actual _merge_diffs on fresh clones of the two stated tensors at weights 0.8/0.8, supplying each returned mode/density/sign; compare using torch.equal. This is not a native Comfy loader or full-size patch hash comparison.

cause: The no_slerp orthogonal early return uses the frequency sign placeholder; basic reaches the ordinary non-TIES total placeholder. Sum and average ignore that parameter, but both candidate signatures and group-cache keys retain it.
implication: A top-three sweep can spend two slots on the same effective linear policy. Three candidate configurations must not be described as three distinct merged behaviors for these sweeps.
limits: The CPU probe establishes identical tiny-tensor results, and real sweeps establish matching complete captured decisions and metrics. No full-size candidate-2/3 tensor hash comparison or controlled timing saving has been performed. A replacement candidate could change the winner; no quality gain is established.
next_action: Prototype canonical keys that ignore only mathematically inactive parameters, initially behind an explicit experiment so disconnected behavior and frozen controls stay unchanged. Retain real TIES voting/density, sparsification, refinement and strength distinctions; regression-test before a new numerical/render study.
